purpose: Independent practice of A10.2 — comparing mass. Used as Lesson 2 consolidation artifact.
student_learning_goal: I can compare how heavy things are.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can compare how heavy things are.
header.character_watermark: Tess the Tiny Mouse in the top-right corner of the header, holding a tiny tape measure. Small (~1.5in tall). References blueprint.recurring_characters.

parts.student_instructions: Look at each pair. Circle the HEAVIER object.
parts.visual_layout: Five paired-object rows stacked vertically. Each row shows two objects: (1) book vs feather, (2) brick vs balloon, (3) shoe vs paper, (4) backpack vs eraser, (5) two same-size blocks. Each pair ~3in × 1.5in.

image_placeholders.description: Five paired-object rows in B&W line art for a Kindergarten worksheet, each row ~3in × 1.5in. Each row shows two contrasting objects for mass comparison. Row 1: book + feather. Row 2: brick + balloon. Row 3: shoe + sheet of paper. Row 4: backpack + eraser. Row 5: two same-size identical blocks. Generous spacing for circling.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS02_P1_PAIRS at Part 1: instructions ask the child to circle the heavier object. Keywords name objects shown that are clearly heavier than their partners.

parts.answer_key: Row 1: book. Row 2: brick. Row 3: shoe. Row 4: backpack. Row 5: SAME — accept circling either or both.

parts.student_instructions: Look at each balance. Write H next to the HEAVIER side. Write L next to the LIGHTER side.
parts.visual_layout: Three balance pictures stacked vertically. Each balance shows two pans, with a different object on each side: (1) apple vs grape, (2) book vs pencil, (3) two same-weight cubes. The pan on the heavier side is drawn lower. Each balance ~3in × 2in. Beside each pan is a small box for the child to write H or L.

image_placeholders.description: Three balance pictures in B&W line art for a Kindergarten worksheet, stacked vertically. Each balance has a triangular fulcrum and two horizontal pans. Balance 1: apple on left (lower) + grape on right (higher). Balance 2: book on left (lower) + pencil on right (higher). Balance 3: two same-weight cubes, balance level (both pans equal height). Each balance ~3in × 2in. Beside each pan, a small empty label box (~0.5in × 0.5in) for the child to write H or L.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS02_P2_BALANCES at Part 2: instructions ask the child to label which side is heavier (H) or lighter (L). Keywords name the visual artifact (balance) and the response options (heavier, lighter).

parts.answer_key: Balance 1: apple = H, grape = L. Balance 2: book = H, pencil = L. Balance 3: both cubes = SAME (accept both H, both L, or both 'same').

parts.part_title: Part 3: Find heavier in your classroom!
parts.student_instructions: Look around your classroom. Pick 2 things. Draw them. Circle the HEAVIER one.
parts.visual_layout: Two blank drawing boxes side by side, each ~3in × 2in with thin solid border. Below each box, a label line for the object's name.

image_placeholders.description: Two blank drawing boxes side by side for a Kindergarten worksheet. Each box is ~3in × 2in with a thin solid border. Below each box, a horizontal line for writing the object's name. Designed for the child to draw two classroom items and circle the heavier.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS02_P3_BOXES at Part 3: instructions ask the child to find and draw two classroom items, circling the heavier. Keywords name the prompt focus (heavier, classroom).

parts.answer_key: Any 2 classroom objects with one clearly heavier. Common: book vs pencil, backpack vs eraser, scissors vs paper.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, find 1 thing LIGHTER than a feather (good luck!).
teacher_notes: Lesson 2 consolidation artifact. Use Part 1 as the formative signal for size-mass conflation — children who circle the bigger but lighter object (e.g., feather over book if feather is drawn larger) need the 'feel, don't guess' re-loop.
